subtopics.name: Practical: Determine the % of Oxygen in Air

parts.problem_md:
This question is about gases in the atmosphere.

The box gives the names of some gases in the atmosphere.

| argon | carbon dioxide | helium | nitrogen | oxygen |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Choose gases from the box to answer these questions. Each gas may be used once, more than once or not at all.

i) Identify a noble gas.

(1)

ii) Identify a gas that makes up about 78% of the atmosphere.

(1)

iii) Identify a greenhouse gas.

(1)

iv) Identify a gas produced by the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate.

(1)
parts.solution_md:
i) A noble gas is:

- Argon / Ar **OR **Helium / He; **[1 mark]**

ii) A gas that makes up about 78% of the atmosphere is:

- Nitrogen / N<sub>2</sub>; **[1 mark]**

iii) A greenhouse gas is:

- Carbon dioxide / CO<sub>2</sub>; **[1 mark]**

iv) A gas produced by the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate is:

- Carbon dioxide / CO<sub>2</sub>; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 4 marks]**

- *You need to know the gases present in the atmosphere together with their percentage abundance*

parts.problem_md:
Sulfur reacts with oxygen to produce sulfur dioxide gas.

i) Write a chemical equation for this reaction.

(1)

ii) State an environmental problem caused when sulfur dioxide gas dissolves in water in the atmosphere.

(1)
parts.solution_md:
i) The chemical equation for when sulfur reacts with oxygen to produce sulfur dioxide gas is:

- S + O<sub>2</sub> → SO<sub>2</sub>; **[1 mark]**

ii) An environmental problem caused when sulfur dioxide gas dissolves in water in the atmosphere is:

- Acid rain **OR **Kills fish / harms aquatic life **OR **Damages plants **OR **Corrodes limestone / marble buildings and statues; **[1 mark]** *Accept other adverse effects of acid rain * *Reference to being toxic / pollutant is ignored*

**[Total: 2 marks]**

- *You need to know that some fossil fuels, especially coal, contain sulfur impurities and why burning such fuels is problematic*

parts.problem_md:
A teacher uses this apparatus to find the percentage of oxygen in a gaseous mixture of oxygen and argon.

![oxygen-composition-of-air-experiment](assets/006-oxygen-composition-of-air-experiment.png)

This is the teacher’s method.

1. Heat the copper powder
2. Push the plunger on syringe A to pass the mixture of oxygen and argon over the hot copper so that the mixture moves into syringe B
3. Push the plunger on syringe B to pass the mixture of oxygen and argon over the hot copper so that the mixture moves into syringe A
4. Record the reading on syringe A
5. Repeat Steps 2, 3 and 4 a number of times

The volume of gas decreases as the oxygen reacts with the copper.

Argon is unreactive so does not react with the copper.

The copper powder turns black.

i) Give a reason why the copper powder is heated.

(1)

ii) State why argon is unreactive.

(1)

iii) Give the name of the black powder that forms when the oxygen reacts with the copper.

(1)
parts.solution_md:
i) A reason why the copper powder is heated is:

- To increase the rate of reaction **OR **To give the particles enough energy to react **OR **Because, cold copper does not react with oxygen **OR **To make the copper react with oxygen; **[1 mark]**

ii) Argon is unreactive because:

- It / argon does not gain / lose / share electrons **OR **It / argon has a full outer shell of electrons; **[1 mark]**

iii) The name of the black powder that forms when the oxygen reacts with the copper is:

- Copper oxide; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *This question draws on knowledge from a number of ideas:*

  - *Rates of reaction - increasing the temperature increases the rate of reaction*
  - *Noble gases - they are known to be unreactive due to their full / complete outer shell of electrons*
  - *Word equations - copper + oxygen → copper oxide*

parts.problem_md:
The table shows the teacher’s results.

| **Reading number** | **Reading on syringe A in cm**<sup>**3**</sup>** ** |
|---|---|
| Start | 78 |
| 1 | 70 |
| 2 | 67 |
| 3 | 65 |
| 4 | 63 |
| 5 | 61 |
| 6 | 60 |
| 7 | 59 |
| 8 | 58 |
| 9 | 58 |
| 10 | 58 |

i) State how the results show that all the oxygen has reacted.

(1)

ii) The volume of gas in the glass tube and connecting tubes is 175 cm<sup>3</sup>.

Calculate the percentage of oxygen in the mixture of oxygen and argon.

(3)

iii) Suggest one reason why the calculated percentage of oxygen in the mixture may not be accurate.

(1)
parts.solution_md:
i) The results show that all the oxygen has reacted because:

- The last results are all the same; **[1 mark]**

ii) The percentage of oxygen in the mixture of oxygen and argon is:

- Volume of oxygen = 20 cm<sup>3</sup>;** [1 mark]**
- Total volume = 253 cm<sup>3</sup>; **[1 mark]**
- Percentage of oxygen = $\frac{20}{253}\times100$ = 7.9%; **[1 mark]** *If the volume of oxygen and / or the total volume are incorrect, the subsequent marks can still be scored by error carried forward* *Correct answer of 7.9% without working scores all 3 marks*

iii) One reason why the calculated percentage of oxygen in the mixture may not be accurate is:

- There may be a leak (in the equipment) **OR **The temperature was not the same for all readings **OR **The equipment was not left to cool (to room temperature);

**[Total: 5 marks]**

- *The volume of oxygen is the amount that the results have decreased by, i.e. 78 → 58 = 20 cm*<sup>*3*</sup>* *
- *The total volume is the 175 cm*<sup>*3*</sup>* of the glass tube and connecting tubes plus the initial 78 cm*<sup>*3*</sup>* in syringe A*
- *A common mistake with this calculation is to get answers over 100%, which is not possible*

  - *If this happens, check the values you are using and check that you have them the correct way up in the division calculation*
- *The results would not be accurate because of issues with the equipment: *

  - *As you are dealing with gases and have equipment with multiple connections, there are likely to be leaks in the equipment*
  - *It cannot be because not all of the oxygen has reacted - all of the oxygen was shown to have reacted in part (i)*

parts.problem_md:
The percentage by volume of oxygen in air can be found by using the rusting of iron. A student sets up this apparatus to measure the volume of oxygen in a sample of air.

![screen-shot-2022-10-10-at-12-55-10](assets/004-screen-shot-2022-10-10-at-12-55-10.png)

An excess of wet iron filings is used. At the start of each experiment, the reading on the syringe is recorded and the apparatus is then left for a week so that the reaction is complete. The reading on the syringe is then recorded again.

The diagram shows the readings in one experiment.

![screen-shot-2022-10-10-at-12-55-16](assets/005-screen-shot-2022-10-10-at-12-55-16.png)

Complete the table to show:

- the syringe reading at the end of this experiment
- the volume of oxygen used in the experiment.

| syringe reading at start / cm<sup>3</sup> | 76 |
|---|---|
| syringe reading at end / cm<sup>3</sup> |   |
| volume of oxygen used / cm<sup>3</sup> |   |
parts.solution_md:
The correct readings are:

| syringe reading at start / cm<sup>3</sup> | 76 |
|---|---|
| syringe reading at end / cm<sup>3</sup> | 35; **[1 mark]** |
| volume of oxygen used / cm<sup>3</sup> | 41; **[1 mark]** |

**[Total: 2 marks] **

parts.problem_md:
The table shows the results recorded by a different student in her experiment.

| volume of air in conical flask / cm<sup>3</sup> | 100 |
|---|---|
| volume of air in connecting tube / cm<sup>3</sup> | 10 |
| original volume of air in syringe / cm<sup>3</sup> | 80 |
| final volume of air in syringe / cm<sup>3</sup> | 43 |

Calculate the percentage of oxygen in air using these results.

percentage of oxygen = ............. %
parts.solution_md:
The percentage of oxygen in air using these results is:

- Calculation of volume of oxygen used; **[1 mark] **
- Calculation of original volume of air; **[1 mark] **
- Calculation of percentage; **[1 mark] ***Example calculation: *80 − 43 = 37 (cm<sup>3</sup>) 100 + 10 + 80 = 190 (cm<sup>3</sup>) `fraction numerator open parentheses 37 space cross times space 100 close parentheses over denominator 190 end fraction space equals space 19`% / 19.47% / 19.5%

**[Total: 3 marks] **

- *It is important to show your working so the examiner can credit you for specific steps and also for any errors that have been carried forward *

parts.problem_md:
The table shows some possible causes of anomalous results in this experiment. Use terms from the box to complete the table, showing possible causes and their effects on the volume of oxygen used in this experiment.

| decreased | increased | no effect |
|---|---|---|

Each term may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

| **Possible cause** | **Effect on volume of oxygen used** |
|---|---|
| wet iron filings not in excess |   |
| apparatus left for 1 hour instead of 1 week |   |
| apparatus left in a warmer place for 1 week |   |
parts.solution_md:
The terms that will be used are:

| **Possible cause** | **Effect on volume of oxygen used** |
|---|---|
| wet iron filings not in excess | Decreased; **[1 mark] ** |
| apparatus left for 1 hour instead of 1 week | Decreased; **[1 mark] ** |
| apparatus left in a warmer place for 1 week | No effect; **[1 mark] ** |

**[Total: 3 marks] **

- *If the iron filings are not in excess the volume of oxygen required will be less than if the iron filings were in excess (as shown in the practical method)*
- *The rusting of iron is a very slow reaction, so if the reaction has less time to proceed, the volume of oxygen used will be less*
- *Leaving the apparatus in a warmer place for the same length of time (a week) will only lead to a faster reaction, the volume of oxygen used will remain unchanged *

parts.problem_md:
The approximate percentage of oxygen in air can be determined in the laboratory using this apparatus.

![2-3-q2-edexcel-igcse-chemistry](assets/001-2-3-q2-edexcel-igcse-chemistry.png)

The steps for the method are shown below.

The steps shown are not in the correct order.

| **Step K:** | Place some damp iron wool and a rubber bung in the top of the tube |
|---|---|
| **Step L:** | Leave the apparatus for a few days |
| **Step M:** | Place a graduated glass tube in a beaker of water |
| **Step N:** | Record the reading of the water level in the tube |
| **Step O:** | Record the reading of the water level again |

Which of the following shows the correct order of the steps above?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A.**

- The correct answer is **A** because these steps would allow the volume of oxygen used during the reaction of iron and oxygen to be found:

  - volume of oxygen used = final reading of the water level - initial reading for the water level
- The percentage of oxygen in air can be calculated:

  - percentage of oxygen in air = (volume of oxygen used ÷ volume of air in tube at start) x 100

parts.problem_md:
A teacher uses the reaction between phosphorus and oxygen to calculate the percentage of oxygen in air. She uses this apparatus and excess phosphorus.

![phosphorus-experiment](assets/002-phosphorus-experiment.png)

The volume of gas in the tube decreases as the phosphorus reacts with oxygen. The teacher measures the volume of gas in the tube at one-minute intervals. The table shows the teacher’s results.

| **Time in minutes** | **Volume of gas in tube in cm**<sup>**3**</sup> |
|---|---|
| 0 | 48.5 |
| 1 | 41.0 |
| 2 | 38.0 |
| 4 | 37.5 |
| 5 | 37.0 |
| 6 | 37.0 |
| 7 | 37.0 |

State how the results show that all the oxygen has reacted.
parts.solution_md:
The results show that all of the oxygen has reacted as:

- Results are the same at the end / there is a constant volume in the tube / the volume of gas stops decreasing / no change after 4 / 5 minutes;** [1 mark] ***Ignore references to time Reject the volume of gas stops increasing*

**[Total: 1 mark]**

- *This is an example of using data from a table rather than a graph, which is the more usual way to present rates information for analysis*

parts.problem_md: Give one change to this experiment that would make the results more accurate.
parts.solution_md:
One change to this experiment that would make the results more accurate is:

- (Use a glass tube / scale with) smaller divisions / with 0.1 cm<sup>3</sup> divisions / a smaller scale; **[1 mark] ***Ignore references to repeating the experiment Ignore references to temperature*

**[Total: 1 mark]**

- *Experimental skills such as understanding accuracy are key to chemistry; accuracy can be improved by making it easier to make a measurement that is as close to the true value as possible, including improving the equipment used*

parts.problem_md:
Use the results to calculate the percentage of oxygen in air. Give your answer to one decimal place.

percentage = ...........................%
parts.solution_md:
The percentage of oxygen in air is:

- Volume of oxygen = 11.5 (cm<sup>3</sup>);** [1 mark]**
- (11.5 ÷ 48.5) x 100; **[1 mark]**
- 23.7; **[1 mark] ***Correct answer to 1 dp with or without working scores 3 marks Allow ecf from M1 M3 must be an answer to 1dp*

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *The volume of oxygen is deduced from the initial volume of gas in the cylinder minus the final volume (48.5 - 37.0), as the oxygen required has been removed from the air*
- *The rest is a percentage calculation of how much oxygen was present compared to the total volume of gas*
- *Read carefully to make sure you get the 1 decimal place mark!*

parts.problem_md:
A student uses this apparatus to investigate the effect of heat on different solid metal carbonates.

![1cr-q5](assets/003-1cr-q5.png)

This is the student’s method:

- Use a spatula to put some metal carbonate in the boiling tube
- Fit the delivery tube into position
- Pour some limewater into the test tube
- Start a timer and immediately begin to heat the metal carbonate
- Record the time when a change first occurs in the limewater

The student repeats the method using different metal carbonates.

When a metal carbonate is heated a reaction sometimes occurs. The equation for the reaction is:

metal carbonate → metal oxide + carbon dioxide

State the name given to this type of reaction.
parts.solution_md:
The name given to this type of reaction is:

- Thermal decomposition;** [1 mark]**

**[Total: 1 mark]**

- *You don't need to have 'thermal' to get the mark*

parts.problem_md:
State two variables that the student should control in this investigation.

1. ........................................... 2. ...........................................

Two variables that the student should control in this investigation:

parts.problem_md: Explain the purpose of limewater in this investigation.

There is a relationship between the position of a metal in the reactivity series and how easily the metal carbonate reacts when heated.

parts.problem_md:
Metal carbonates undergo thermal decomposition when heated.

Which is a correct balanced symbol equation for the thermal decomposition of a metal carbonate?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is D.**

- The correct answer is **D** because when metal carbonates undergo thermal decomposition, a* *metal oxide and carbon dioxide are produced

  - The equation gives the correct formulae of the metal carbonate and metal oxide and it is balanced
- **A** is incorrect as the correct formula of lithium carbonate is Li<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> as the lithium ion has 1+ charge and the carbonate ion has a 2- charge.

  - The correct formula of lithium oxide is Li<sub>2</sub>O  as the oxide ion has a 2- charge
- **B** is incorrect as the correct formula of magnesium carbonate is MgCO<sub>3</sub> as the magnesium ion has 2+ charge and the carbonate ion has a 2- charge.

  - The correct formula of magnesium oxide is MgO as the oxide ion has a 2- charge
- **C** is incorrect as carbon dioxide is produced in thermal decomposition, it is not a reactant

parts.problem_md:
Combustion reactions involve a chemical change in which oxygen reacts with elements or compounds to produce oxides.

Which is the correct statement about combustion?

| ☐ | **A** | Combustion reactions are also reduction reactions |
|---|---|---|
| ☐ | **B** | During the combustion of sulfur, a blue flame is observed and a colourless, poisonous gas is produced |
| ☐ | **C** | All combustion reactions are endothermic |
| ☐ | **D** | The balanced symbol equation for the combustion of hydrogen is: H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> |
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B.**

- The correct answer is **B** because aulfur reacts with oxygen during a combustion reaction forming sulfur dioxide

  - S (s) + O<sub>2</sub> (g) → SO<sub>2</sub> (g)
  - A blue flame is seen and sulfur dioxide is a colourless, poisonous gas
- A is incorrect as combustion reactions are also classified as oxidation reactions
- C is incorrect as combustion reactions are all exothermic as heat is released
- D is incorrect as water (not hydrogen peroxide, H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>) is produced during the combustion of hydrogen, 2H<sub>2 </sub>+ O<sub>2 </sub>→ 2H<sub>2</sub>O
